data.narrative:
Stellaria is a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Nicolas Breyton and backed by CEA and Schneider Electric. It has raised €23M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 11 peers across nuclear energy—3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Applied Atomics.

A peer-median approach is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables; only one private nuclear peer exists at a comparable stage, below the three-company threshold needed for statistical reliability. Consequently, stage-progression methodology is the primary valuation lens. Using total raised ($23M) as a value proxy and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $58M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $49M to $66M, centered on $58M. This range reflects a ±15% band around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the narrowness of the peer set and the limited direct comparability of seed-stage nuclear ventures, which typically face heterogeneous technology and regulatory risk profiles. A more robust triangulation would require additional private-market transaction data within nuclear energy or broader deep-tech infrastructure sectors. Management quality and institutional backing (CEA, Schneider Electric) provide downside support but require separate assessment beyond quantitative methods applied here.
